# Expertise Summary For Restructure project-manager agent + issue-managing skill, remove overlap/duplicates, run tests ≥85%, optimize slowness

## Mental Model

**Agent system files** live in `.claude/agents/` as Markdown. The two artifacts this task touches are tightly coupled and currently hold DUPLICATED content:
- `.claude/agents/project-manager.md` — the agent under test. Operational patterns (work-loop mechanics, sync tracker, hierarchy/tags, phase flows, three loops, cross-team patterns, special scenarios) are **inlined directly in this file** because of the preload limitation below.
- `.claude/skills/issue-managing/SKILL.md` — created as a "synced reference" that duplicates the operational content verbatim. Per stored expertise, these two files are explicitly kept in sync and contain the same operational content. **This duplication is the core of the task's "remove overlap" instruction** — the human previously pushed back on skill bloat and asked for "concise with clear rules" (283 → 196 lines).

**The split the task is asking for is the *intended* design:** agent file = personality/responsibility; skill = rules for managing issues. The reason content got inlined into the agent file is the preload limitation (see Business Rules).

**Test suite shape:** `project-manager` suite = 27 scenarios in `.agentic/project-manager-suite/01..27-*.md` + `00-team-roster.md` + `README.md`. Runner is `test-runner.ts` (Bun/TS); usage in `testing.md`; results in `test-results/`. Suite currently passes **27/27 at ≥85%, avg ~66/70 (~95%)** as of 2026-06-14.

## Business Rules And Invariants

- **🚨 CRITICAL — `skills:` frontmatter does NOT preload when the agent runs via `claude --agent` from the CLI.** It only preloads for subagents launched via the Task tool from a parent session. In test mode (`--tools ""`) the agent CANNOT invoke skills at all. **This is the central constraint for the restructuring:** if you move operational rules OUT of the agent file and INTO the skill only, the test-mode agent will no longer see them and scores will collapse. Any restructure that splits "rules live in the skill" MUST keep the rules also inlined in the agent file (or the runner must inject them), or tests will fail. This was the root cause of 5+ hours of fruitless edits.
- **Hierarchy/scoring criteria live in THREE places that must stay aligned:** the agent prompt, the skill (verbatim copy), AND the judge's `hierarchy` dimension in `test-runner.ts` (`JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, ~line 275). Plus every scenario's Expected Output tree, plus hierarchy sections in `00-team-roster.md` and `README.md`. A 2026-06-14 refactor touched 8 files in lockstep. When restructuring, grep ALL of these.
- **The test runner injects `AGENTRACK_CLI_REF` via `--append-system-prompt`** which can conflict with agent/skill content (lists `sync` as a standalone tag, shows `agt blockages resolve` — both of which the PM skill says to ignore). Check what the runner injects before relying on it.
- **Keep skills CONCISE and rule-based; fix bloat by deleting, not only adding.** The user explicitly pushed back on an over-long `issue-managing` skill and asked for "concise with clear rules" (283 → 196 lines). When the skill grows past a few hundred lines, look for redundancy and merge/delete before adding. The same concision applies to the agent system prompt. **This directly maps to the task's "reduce verbosity, remove duplicates" instruction** — the expected fix style is cut/merge, not append.
- **Judge variance:** the sonnet judge has ±5–10 point run-to-run swing on individual scenarios. A scenario at 84% may re-run at 93%. Before adding rules to lift a borderline scenario, re-run it — it may be variance, not a real gap.
- **Testing mode = no side effects.** The agent returns a PLAN; it must not mutate issues. Enforced at CLI level (`--tools ""`), not in the agent file. Do not change this.

## Recipes

- **`bun .agentic/project-manager-suite/test-runner.ts`** — the runner. Flags relevant to the "run tests ≥85%" step: `--list` (confirm scenario count + CLI health, no run); `--scenario NN` (single-scenario smoke test); `--verbose` (per-step detail, pairs with `--scenario`); `--no-judge` / `--judge-only` (two-phase: collect PM responses cheaply, then score without re-running the expensive PM agent).
- **`bun .agentic/project-manager-suite/validate-skill.ts`** — validates agent + skill frontmatter. Use after editing `.claude/agents/project-manager.md` or `issue-managing/SKILL.md`.
- **`bun .agentic/project-manager-suite/inspect.ts NN`** — prints a single scenario's tags, blockages, status-updates, and sync-tracker reasoning. Essential for diagnosing WHY a scenario failed during story-by-story iteration.
- **`bun .agentic/project-manager-suite/show-scores.ts`** — quick overview of all current scores.
- **`bun .agentic/project-manager-suite/regenerate-summary.ts`** — rebuild `summary.json` after piecemeal `--scenario NN` re-runs (single-scenario runs do NOT rewrite `summary.json`).
- **Story-by-story iteration workflow** (user explicitly preferred this over batch runs, and it is the proven fix loop): run ONE scenario → inspect the agent's literal response → identify the WRONG mental model behind the failure → add a targeted rule that names and debunks that specific misconception → re-test that one scenario → repeat. Use this after restructuring to confirm each scenario still passes before doing a full run.

## Timeline Context

- **2026-06-13**: Built `issue-managing` skill + iterated PM agent from 33% → 100% pass (all 27 ≥85%, avg ~94%). Inlined operational content into `project-manager.md` because `skills:` frontmatter doesn't preload in CLI mode. User pushed back on skill length → condensed 283→196 lines by deleting/restructuring.
- **2026-06-14**: Refactored hierarchy model top-down ("cross-team = 4 levels / never skip levels") → bottom-up ("no single-child parents"). Touched 8 files in lockstep (agent, skill, 3 stories, roster, README, judge prompt). Lesson: a single hierarchy rule is duplicated across agent prompt AND skill (verbatim), and the judge encodes its own copy — all three + scenario Expected Outputs must be edited together. **This is directly relevant: the "remove overlap" instruction targets exactly this verbatim duplication.**

## Gaps And Verification Needs

- The expertise-manager cannot read files under `.agentic/project-manager-suite/` (access-restricted). The requesting claude-developer must verify runner code/flags live. Details confirmed against live code on 2026-06-13 (27 scenarios, 7 dimensions, `claude` 2.1.177).
- **On the "agent is slow to reply" optimization sub-task:** the stored expertise has NO analysis of agent reply latency. The only related facts captured are runner-side timeouts (600 s per PM call, 300 s per judge, raised from 300/120 s after ETIMEDOUT failures) and a cost estimate (~60–90 min for a full 27×2-call suite, up to ~3 h worst case, ~5 min PM + ~2 min judge per scenario). **There is no stored expertise on prompt-length/verbosity as a latency cause** — this must be investigated fresh. Given the agent file currently has inlined operational content (verbosity the task wants to reduce), prompt length is a plausible lever, but that is reasoning, not stored expertise.
- Re-scan `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/` for the current file set before editing; the agent list may have drifted.
